messages:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed a big spike in console chart frame time after the eu-canary went out ~10:30. 2–3s on sparklines now.
Mira: ugh sorry saw alerts, digging. any trace IDs?
Alex: laptop attached a quick flame sample: main thread blocked while parsing chunk from streamer-lite. Looks correlated with telemetry client import + kvcache evictions.
Sam: wait streamer-lite was only meant for streaming traces not charts. which bundle included it?
Jules: the canary rolled frontend@v2026.03.10 which added streaming-telemetry -> streamer-lite v1.4. small bundle delta but changes import timing.
deploy-bot: deploy started: frontend-v2026.03.10 canary -> 10% eu region (by routing weight)
Mira: routing weight increased eu traffic, and we had prefetch window widened in the same release — that could bump kvcache pressure. if prefetch + streaming import happen, parse thrash.
Alex: logs show kvcache miss bursts when many small chart requests hit concurrently, followed by heavy script parse. kvcache eviction metric jumped 4x at 10:31.
Sam: so two factors: (1) streamer-lite triggers big init on first import, (2) prefetch flooding causes more cold imports because kvcache evicts bundles.
Jules: telemetry sampling also changed in the release — default went from 1% -> 5% for debug traces. that makes telemetry client do more work on render path.
Mira: action plan: roll back streamer-lite import (quick), tighten prefetch window for canary users, and reduce telemetry sampling for canary group.
Alex: agree. quick rollback would be fastest to confirm root cause. can we hotfix to lazy-load streamer-lite only for trace view?
Sam: lazy-load is fine. patch: replace `import "streamer-lite"` with `const s = await import("streamer-lite")` behind feature flag `telemetry_streaming` and gate by route.
Jules: we can ship that as a patch to canary (patch 2026.03.10-1). I'll open a PR.
Mira: also propose increasing kvcache capacity for canary pods by +20% to avoid eviction cascade while we test. ops ok with that?
Alex: ops confirmed we can bump kvcache memory for a short window. I'll coordinate.
Sam: also check bundler splitpoints — streamer-lite ended up in the same chunk as `chart-core` due to import graph. splitting it into its own async chunk should keep chart-critical path small.
Jules: yep adding a rollup dynamic import and manual chunk name should do it. will add to PR.
deploy-bot: canary patch PR opened: PR #4281 frontend: lazy-load streamer-lite + telemetry sampling revert
Mira: after patch/rollout let's monitor LCP, frame_time_95, and kvcache_evictions. set a short dashboard with 1m granularity.
Alex: created a temporary dashboard link: https://console.internal/dashboards/quick/6945 (small sample: lcp, frame95, kv_evictions, telemetry_rate)
Sam: thumbs up. if metrics improve we can roll the fix to stable and follow up with a proper chunking release and prefetch tuning.
Jules: FYI I'll also run a local canary that simulates high prefetch concurrency to reproduce. post results later.
Mira: thanks all — moving to rollback now. :thumbsup:
Alex: :eyes: watching metrics.
Sam: will follow up with a brief postmortem note in #postmortems if rollback confirmed cause.
Jules: added test plan in PR for chunk split and lazy import.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: frontend-v2026.03.10-1 canary patch -> 10% eu region
Alex: frame_time95 dropped from 3s -> 0.6s in 2 minutes after patch. looks like streamer-lite import was the culprit.
Mira: closing loop: we'll keep sampling at 1% for now, and schedule a proper bundle-split release next week.
Sam: nice. also flagging routing policy: avoid increasing eu routing weight concurrently with large client-side lib imports. add to rollout checklist.
Jules: added checklist item and a gating rule to the rollout playbook.
Alex: thanks everyone.
